text: COSTUME_SILLA_ATTENDANT_A01 V02 (evidence-corrected, CLM_SILLA_COSTUME_021-031): Silla funeral attendant, 5th to early 6th century. ONE evenly woven, better-bleached plain-weave jacket, hip length or slightly longer, LONG sleeves to the wrist with clean plain cuffs, straight collar crossed shallowly (right over left or left over right), no ribbon ties; medium-width plain trousers; a neat plain cloth belt, no metal plaques, no pendants; low shoes; hair in a neat topknot, bare or with a plain cloth band; off-white, light grey or grey-brown tones, clean and tidy. MORE items than a labourer, far fewer than the elite observer: no silk, no cap of rank, no metal belt, no ankle boots. Forbidden: short sleeves, futou hat, round-collar danryeong, bronze or iron belt buckle, metal plaques, Joseon hanbok silhouette, ribbon ties, official colours. The collar closes with the belt only; no dangling chest tie or ribbon-like cord at the collar (seen in 09-17 samples).
